correctness.rationale: Rescale to common rate one. Explicit conditional density Hθ/Zθ has positive interior support. The cross-partial sign determines the sharp likelihood-ratio phase for θ≥0 versus θ<0; exact expansion N_s Z−N Z_s into three strictly negative components for θ≤0 gives strict conditional-CDF monotonicity. Positive θ uses LR⇒ST. Exchangeability and quantile reflection yield strict coordinatewise vector coupling. Endpoints θ=±1 and all sum and threshold ranges covered. Symbolic identities independently expanded; finite script checks supplement, not replace, universal proof.

value.rationale: Strong Efron conditional risk monotonicity under dependence is an explicitly studied mathematical problem. The theorem gives a sharp entire-copula-parameter classification for the likelihood-ratio relation while proving unexpectedly robust strict vector usual-order monotonicity at every negative dependence strength. Earlier uniform-margin FGM results exhibit a different regime, so the observed dependence on marginal transformations is structurally meaningful. No extrapolation to unequal rates or arbitrary copulas is implied.
